Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so our infra team can put together a sizing plan: 

1) Recap of needs
- Primary use case: customer-facing chat with incremental streaming of responses
- Latency SLO: p95 user-facing ~250-300ms (you mentioned 250ms target)
- Expectation of high concurrency during promo windows (you estimated a big spike)

2) Missing items we need to finalize sizing (can fill the attached template):
- Average request size (tokens in) and average response size (tokens out)
- Typical tokens generated per exchange (sum of in+out)
- QPS / steady-state vs peak QPS (please give an explicit "peak hour" definition and a burst multiplier)
- Concurrent open sessions (concurrency during peak)
- Percentage of requests that require streaming vs batch/async
- Any hard p99 or cold-start limits we should be aware of

I've attached a short template (throughput_requirements_template.xlsx) — if you can drop numbers in there that will speed things up.

Next step: Can we schedule a 30–45 minute technical sizing call next week with Marissa (Solutions/infra) so we can map these numbers to model variants, batching strategy, and autoscale policies? Proposed agenda: workload characterization, token/sec estimate, streaming implications, and fallback policies.

Thanks — I can be flexible on time.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex / Redwood inference

Rafael —

Thanks for the template, attaching a short usage snapshot for June (usage_report_June.pdf). Answers inline below and in the attached: 

- Average request (tokens in): ~80 tokens (user messages tend to be short)
- Average response (tokens out): ~240 tokens (long-form explanations)
- Typical tokens/exchange: ~320 tokens
- Steady-state QPS: ~12 QPS (global average across business hours)
- Peak QPS (peak hour): ~80 QPS (we define "peak hour" as the busiest rolling 60 minutes during day-of events)
- Concurrency at peak: roughly 200 concurrent open sessions (many sessions are streaming with long-lived connections)
- Streaming: yes — ~80% of live chat requests are streamed (we send partial transcripts to client as soon as model emits tokens)
- p95 latency target: 250ms end-to-end for first token when streaming; for non-streaming/batch responses 1–2s is acceptable

A few other notes: we rely on a high degree of freshness for embeddings and will likely want a cache warm strategy to reduce cold-starts. Also interested in model variants — we prefer something that matches performance of gpt-4o-style open models but we'd like Redwood's recommendations on cost/latency tradeoffs.

Let me know when you and Marissa are available for the technical sizing call.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Director of Product
Finex Payments

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Alex —

This is great, thanks for the details and the June snapshot. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock the sizing call: 

- Streaming: when you say p95 250ms for first token, is that measured from client send to first token received by client, or do you have additional network hops (CDN/mobile) to include? We typically size for "first-token" latency at the model-runtime boundary and include a 50–100ms buffer for transport where appropriate.

- Percent streaming: you noted 80% — is that consistent during peak hour as well, or is streaming mostly during steady-state?

- Burst multiplier: for planning, do you expect the 80 QPS peak to be a single sustained hour or multiple bursts? If you have any historical peak multipliers (e.g., 3x sustained bursts for 10–15 minutes) that helps with autoscale configuration.

Proposed next step: Marissa and I will run a quick internal model/instance estimate mapping from your numbers (tokens/sec and concurrency) and then propose two options: (A) cost-optimized (larger batch sizes / slightly relaxed 1st-token latency) and (B) latency-optimized (dedicated capacity, smaller batches, guaranteed p95). We'll cover both in the sizing call and provide a short deliverable with recommended instance counts, expected p95 latencies, and cost estimates.

If that sounds good I'll send a couple of times for the call.

Best,
Rafael
